content.text: The bug is in `parseDate`: `Date.UTC` takes a 0-based month, but the ISO month is 1-based, so every date is parsed a month late.

content.content: The file /work/.tmp/claude-eval-o8uTx7/home/cwd/src/dates.js has been updated successfully.

lines: // Parse an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) into a UTC Date.

content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `parseDate` in `src/dates.js`. It passed the 1-based ISO month straight into `Date.UTC`, which expects a 0-based month. Every parsed date landed one month late, so a Jan 30 invoice with net-14 terms came out due 2026-03-16 instead of 2026-02-13. I changed it to `Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d)`, and `npm test` now passes.

`src/report.js` also calls `parseDate`, so its output was shifted by a month too and is now correct. I didn't check the report code beyond that call.

Any invoices already sent with wrong due dates will need to be identified and corrected separately. I haven't touched any stored data.
